title: Communication weirdo
summary: Natalie Karolak explains her direct, brief communication style - which colleagues often interpret as rude or bossy - as stemming from how she processes language, not from malice. She describes years of effort to improve body language and tone, and requests direct feedback when her communication misses the mark.
key_points: The author's tone often sounds harsh or bossy unintentionally; what listeners interpret as hidden meaning is usually just blunt expression with no subtext.
Years of training improved her spoken communication and body language, but written messages remain terse and can misfire despite proofreading and rephrasing.
She processes language differently in writing versus speech, prefers telegraphic style in written text, and relies on emojis to convey tone more accurately than words.
Direct, immediate feedback helps her improve; she interprets messages literally and values honesty over social cushioning in communication.

quotes.text: My answers are very short and direct. What I'm asking from you sounds harsh because I try to use as little words as possible.
quotes.why_it_matters: Identifies the specific communication pattern that triggers misinterpretation.
